classification_definitions.integration: A real production filesystem, service, network or store boundary materially supports target assertion.
classification_definitions.unit: Local predicate/serialization/crypto or synthetic handler/store; incidental file/process setup receives no boundary credit.
classification_definitions.mixed: Separate independent real-boundary and local-only assertion blocks.
classification_definitions.unresolved: Insufficient or contradictory mapped/connected source; distinct from runtime UNKNOWN.

roots.reason: Root-key PEM/seed rejection uses a local byte/key predicate before staging, with an independent output-absent check. The unrelated-key acceptance block reaches EmitPacket real staging writes, full read/hash validation, no-replace rename, and final destination validation; its success materially depends on the emitted filesystem packet. No guest runtime installation is exercised.

The target is maxSourcePins acceptance/rejection in Manifest.Validate. Real signed packet files supply decoded inputs and successful validation also reads fixture files, but no source inventory file is checked or changed: the padded pins are synthetic strings. Filesystem setup is incidental to the inventory-count predicate.

The test mutates FileEntry.Size and a synthetic Routes slice and calls Manifest.Validate directly. Both empty-body and aggregate-size assertions are local schema predicates. packetFixture disk creation supplies unrelated setup only.

All mutation-table assertions reject local manifest path, identity, duplicate or binary metadata contradictions in Manifest.Validate; the final whitespace case rejects canonical serialized bytes. Disk writes/readback deliver those inputs to the decoder, without asserting production file contents or a persistence effect. No actual OCI/guest boundary is exercised.

Unlisted-file, changed executable and symlink blocks change actual packet filesystem state and ValidatePacket walks/opens/hashes it to reject the state. The independent wrong-trusted-root block asserts local signature authorization on a synthetic envelope/keyring; its surrounding disk fixture is incidental.

Zero/future/stale run-clock inputs assert local guards; fixture files only deliver decoded inputs. The final +2h case is also rejected by the earlier +/-5minute fixture-clock guard, before trust.VerifyCurrent. Its intended expired-signature assertion is masked and explicitly uncredited; other clock obligations remain supported by source. No real elapsed-time or external trust boundary is established.

roots.reason: Executable bytes and simulator response bytes are read through production accessors; actual post-validation file tampering is then detected by fresh file digest/size checks. Separate missing-slot and empty other-controller inventory assertions are local selection guards. Path/ownership checks scope copies but do not install a guest.

The target is defensive copying of Manifest arrays and unchanged metadata in derived authorized views after mutating a returned value. Manifest clones and slot/route metadata selection are local. GuestFiles/SimulatorRoutes read unchanged fixture bodies, but no body, file mutation, persisted effect or external authorization source supports the asserted copy-isolation predicates; those file reads are incidental.

assertion_evidence.text:
root, _, _, roots := packetFixture(t)
	packet, err := ValidatePacket(root, roots, time.Now().UTC())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	manifest := packet.Manifest()
	manifest.Controllers[2].Slot = "controller-a"
	manifest.Files[0].Path = "signing/root.key"
	manifest.Files[0].OwnerRole = "root:controller-a"
	manifest.Files[0].Mode = 0o777
	manifest.Routes[0].ControllerSlot = "controller-a"
	manifest.Routes[0].Host = "untrusted.example"
	manifest.Routes[0].BodyPath = "signing/root.key"
	manifest.SourcePins[0].SHA256 = strings.Repeat("0", 64)
	again := packet.Manifest()
	if again.Controllers[2].Slot != "controller-c" || again.Files[0].Path == "signing/root.key" ||
		again.Files[0].Mode == 0o777 || again.Routes[0].Host != "iaas.sa-saopaulo-1.oraclecloud.com" ||
		again.Routes[0].ControllerSlot != "controller-c" || again.SourcePins[0].SHA256 == strings.Repeat("0", 64) {
		t.Fatal("verified packet manifest exposed mutable authorization state")
	}
	files, err := packet.GuestFiles("controller-a")
	if err != nil || len(files) == 0 || files[0].File.OwnerRole != "root:controller-a" {
		t.Fatalf("manifest mutation changed guest copy list: %+v, %v", files, err)
	}
	reads, _, err := packet.SimulatorRoutes("controller-c")
	if err != nil || len(reads) != 1 || reads[0].Host != "iaas.sa-saopaulo-1.oraclecloud.com" {
		t.Fatalf("manifest mutation changed simulator inventory: %+v, %v", reads, err)
	}

roots.reason: The asserted target is strict config Version equality/canonical decode using local byte/map inputs. productionGuestTestInputs creates credentials via a go-run helper and reads files, but that process is incidental setup; validateControllerConfig only decodes and compares in-memory configuration and credential maps. No production controller is started.

CapturedObjectRoute creates route metadata and obtains an SDK-escaped RequestURI by constructing an HTTP request. It never dispatches the request. Exact URI and digest are local serialization/mapping assertions on synthetic CapturedObject bytes.

Public signed history/ledger methods are real code, but the injected CapturingObjectStorage is explicitly an in-memory map. Its PutObject/GetObject exchange synthetic response structs and byte readers; PutCount and completed slot proofs observe this map, with no actual Object Storage, network or durable store boundary. Synthetic signatures establish local validation only.

CurrentCompletedSourcePins discovers actual repository source directories with WalkDir and opens/hashes their real files, then VerifyCompletedSourcePins rediscovers the inventory. Required-file membership and omitted-pin rejection depend on this real discovered source tree and its file reads. No build/execution or source provenance authenticity is established.

Actual current/changed file digests and the replaced symlink ancestor are observed through production Lstat/EvalSymlinks/Open/hash checks. Independent incomplete-inventory and invalid-digest predicates are local. The traversal-path mutation removes one mandatory pin and is rejected by the earlier required-inventory guard, so traversal-specific rejection is masked/uncredited. Mixed category remains supported by the actual file-state blocks and independent local guards.

VerifySourcePins73-76 rejects the omitted required path before reaching the canonical/path-order/digest guard92-94. Traversal-specific coverage remains unresolved/uncredited; the mixed category is independently supported.

roots.reason: Host-root slash rejection is an independent pre-I/O path guard. Plain-directory and symlink cases use actual filesystem metadata: Lstat/EvalSymlinks and parent/root device comparison reject a non-mount/alias. No ext4 mounted guest success or image staging is exercised.

The production account verifier reads actual temporary etc/passwd and etc/group files through safe ancestor/regular-file checks. Both numeric-identity mismatch rejection and matching acceptance depend on parsed bytes returned by those filesystem reads. No guest account lookup service or process is started.

The OCI SDK provider and service clients are real, but every request uses simulatorDispatcher.Do, which clones the request and invokes ServeHTTP against httptest.NewRecorder without dialing. IMDS, federation, token, Compute, Object Storage, missing/unlisted and audit assertions all consume synthetic in-memory handlers/maps. No actual OCI or HTTP exchange is claimed.

httptest.NewServer starts a real loopback HTTP server; server.Client().Do sends the signed federation request through net/http. Status and bounded returned token assertions depend on parsed network response bytes; token helper checks that same returned token against the session/public-key state. Only host-local HTTP interoperability with synthetic IAM materials is established.

Federation and signed exact GET/error cases invoke ServeHTTP directly using ResponseRecorder, then inspect local response and audit map state. RSA signing and token verification are local operations; there is no server/client dialing or real service/store boundary.

Two locally generated key/session pairs and signed query cases use federate/direct recorder calls and in-memory route/session maps. Distinct tokens, exact-query acceptance and changed-target rejection are local handler/crypto predicates without a network exchange.

Oversized route bytes are a local addRead guard; session and audit capacities are populated directly in simulator maps/slices, then direct ResponseRecorder calls assert bounded errors/counts. No actual saturation of a server, network or external store is exercised.

packet_views.text:
func (packet VerifiedPacket) Manifest() Manifest {
	manifest := packet.manifest
	manifest.Controllers = slices.Clone(manifest.Controllers)
	manifest.Files = slices.Clone(manifest.Files)
	manifest.Routes = slices.Clone(manifest.Routes)
	manifest.SourcePins = slices.Clone(manifest.SourcePins)
	return manifest
}

qualification_limits: Packet emission and validation exercise only temporary local filesystem effects and signed synthetic material; no Firecracker, guest startup, cloud API, installed production secret or offline signing-key custody qualification.
Mount guard tests reject actual plain directories/symlinks and a local host-root predicate; no actual mounted ext4 image success is claimed.
Config-version setup contains a subprocess invocation, incidental to local version validation; this review did not invoke it.
CapturingObjectStorage and simulatorDispatcher remain in-memory fakes even with production Ledger and OCI SDK clients; direct ResponseRecorder tests receive no network credit.
Only the specified simulator loopback HTTP root crosses net/http; synthetic IAM keys/certificates/tokens do not establish OCI compatibility beyond the asserted local exchange.
Current source-pin inventory reads actual repository files in the source test design; this review performs source inspection only and does not execute that inventory walker.
No source/repository/shared-ledger mutation, count promotion, deletion, retirement, runtime qualification or global completion credit. All safety obligations retained.
